_comment: CallX — Firebase Realtime Database Security Rules (Linked Devices Module)
_deploy: Merge the 'rules' section below into your existing Firebase DB rules, then: firebase deploy --only database
_instructions: 1. Open your existing merged rules file (or the Firebase Console → Realtime Database → Rules tab).
2. Merge the 'pairingSessions' and 'linkedDevices' (nested under 'users') blocks below into it.
• pairingSessions/{code} is intentionally readable/writable by ANY authenticated OR anonymous
client — the desktop/web companion is not signed in yet when it creates this node, and the
phone needs to read it after just scanning a QR (no prior relationship to that code).
The only sensitive field is 'customToken', and only the Cloud Function (Admin SDK, bypasses
rules entirely) is allowed to WRITE it — rules below explicitly forbid client writes to it.
• 'status' can only move pending -> approved|denied by an authenticated user (the phone),
and only 'uid'-that-approved may ever be written into a given pairing session once.
• users/{uid}/linkedDevices is private to that account: only auth.uid === uid may read/write it,
same as every other per-account node in this schema (blocks, mutes, FCM tokens, etc).
• A linked device's own row can be deleted only by the account owner (revoke), never by the
companion session itself — the web client can only update its own 'lastActiveAt' heartbeat.
• Nothing here changes any existing chat/message/reel/etc. rules: once the web client signs in
with the custom token, auth.uid equals the real account uid, so every rule that already
checks auth.uid (see firebase_chat_rules.json) applies identically — the companion session
is indistinguishable from the phone at the data layer, by design.
